headline: RBI consolidates White Label ATM Operator Directions, 2026; 11 older circulars repealed
summary_points: RBI has consolidated its instructions on White Label ATM Operators (WLAOs) into the RBI (White Label ATM Operators) Directions, 2026, effective immediately.
Issued under Section 18 read with Section 10(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007; 11 earlier circulars from 2012 to 2026 stand repealed.
WLAOs must file the monthly return WLA Statistics (R330) on the CIMS portal by the 7th of the following month.

rows: At least ₹100 crore as per last audited balance sheet, maintained at all times
Post-audit infusion allowed with a Chartered Accountant certificate
Metro/urban : semi-urban : rural at least 1:2:3; reviewed at least once in six months
All ATMs to process EMV chip and PIN cards
WLAs cannot charge bank customers directly; fee only from banks
Direct purchase from RBI Issue Offices/Currency Chests above 1 lakh pieces
More than one sponsor bank permitted; tri-partite SLA required
Return R330 monthly on CIMS by the 7th of next month

who_is_affected: Authorised White Label ATM Operators, sponsor banks, scheduled commercial and co-operative banks, and ATM/card payment network operators.
action_required: WLAOs and sponsor banks should review operations and SLAs against the consolidated Directions and ensure R330 monthly filing on CIMS by the 7th.

RBI has issued the Reserve Bank of India (White Label ATM Operators) Directions, 2026 on November 27, 2026, consolidating its earlier instructions on White Label ATMs.

Key points:
- Effective immediately; issued under Section 18 read with Section 10(2) of the PSS Act, 2007.
- Net worth of at least ₹100 crore to be maintained at all times.
- ATM deployment to maintain a minimum 1:2:3 ratio across metro/urban, semi-urban and rural regions.
- WLAs cannot charge bank customers directly.
- Monthly return R330 to be filed on CIMS by the 7th of the succeeding month.
- 11 earlier circulars issued between 2012 and 2026 stand repealed.

WLAOs, sponsor banks and network operators should map their current arrangements, SLAs and reporting processes to the new Directions.

Please verify the details with the official RBI source before acting.
